plan: Given my value of $25, I need to consider how to maximize profit. Since I pay the second-highest bid, bidding my true value is a good starting point as it guarantees a non-negative profit if I win. However, to maximize profit, I should try to win at a price lower than my value. I will bid slightly above what I expect others to bid, but not exceeding my value. Since this is the first round and I have no history, I'll assume others are rational and might bid close to their values. I will bid my value to avoid losing profit.

My goal is to maximize profit. Since I pay the second-highest bid, I want to bid just enough to win. The other bidders are rational and will also try to maximize their profit. While I don't have historical data for this specific round, I know my value is $18. I will bid slightly above what I perceive to be a conservative estimate of the other bidders' potential bids, but not exceeding my value. I'll aim for a bid that gives me a good chance to win while maintaining a positive profit margin.

[ This is a first-price sealed-bid auction with a second-price payment rule (Vickrey auction). In such auctions, the dominant strategy is to bid your true value. Bidding below your value risks losing to a bid lower than your value, while bidding above your value risks winning and paying more than your value. Since this is the first round and there's no history to learn from, and given the nature of the auction, I will bid my true value. ]
